diagnoses.name: Anaemia
diagnoses.text1:
1. Limit blood loss and supportive care

- Stop any active bleeding
- Keep warm
- Support feeding
diagnoses.text2:
2. Send FBC, Group and cross match

- Evaluate causes
diagnoses.text3:
3. Consider blood transfusion if...

- Severe anaemia - paper white appearance
- Associated respiratory distress
- Signs of heart failure
- if infant symptomatic or underlying condition likely to benefit from increased Hb give transfusion

For acute blood loss: replace estimate loss

For more chronic anaemia (from multiple samples or anaemia of prematurity) use the formula: amount required (mls packed cells)= weight (kg) x desired increase in Hb x 3. 

10-15 ml/kg of packed cells is unlikely to go wrong. 

Rate: 5-10ml/kg/hour.

1ml/kg frusemide should be given one hour after the start or halfway through.
If >15ml/kg calculated volume, consider splitting over consecutive days especially if there is a PDA

Prescribe iron but not if the baby has high fever & sepsis - wait for acute infection to settle

diagnoses.name: Congenital Abnormality
diagnoses.text1:
Includes:
Neural tube defect 
Cleft palate 

1. Refer to surgeons
Specifically refer to orthopaedics for bone injuries or abnormalities
diagnoses.text2:
2. Treat for sepsis / risk of sepsis 

If there is any fever 38.0 or more treat with antibiotics 
Neural tube defects are high risk for sepsis and meningitis
Prophylactic antibiotics may be appropriate
diagnoses.text3:
3. Counselling 

Discuss sensitively how antenatal folate treatment can prevent another neural tube defect in subsequent pregnancies.

diagnoses.name: Consider Congenital Heart Disease
diagnoses.text1:
Cyanosis/bradycardia at birth should be assumed to be RESPIRATORY not cardiac

Cardiac lesions causing poor conditions at birth are rare (e.g. Ebstein's anomaly or arrhythmia with hydrops)

Cardiac lesions can present when babies are hours/days old. 

1. Keep warm, monitor and feed

Monitor oxygen saturations. 

Consider treating for sepsis if requiring significant support

Use naso/orogastric feeds to decrease work of breathing

Organise an Echo and CXR

Monitor for signs of heart failure and consider diuretics
diagnoses.text2:
2. Duct Dependent for systemic blood flow

If left sided obstructive duct dependent heart disease suspected (e.g. hypoplastic left heart or aortic stenosis) 
- Insert a UVC
- Commence prostaglandin infusion at 10 nanograms/kg/min or PO 0.01-0.02 mg/kg/dose by NGT

- Aim for O2 saturations of >75%. Reduce inspired O2 if sats >85%
diagnoses.text3:
3. Duct Dependent Cyanotic Lesions

These include pulmonary atresia and critical pulmonary stenosis

Aim for sats >75%
- commence a prostaglandin as above
- if develops apnoeas or if sats <75% despite prostaglandin, ventilation should be initiated.
- if apnoeas but sats >75%, reduce prostaglandin, but not below 5 ng/kg/min.

diagnoses.name: Convulsions
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Convulsions seen on examination or history
diagnoses.text1:
1. Airway management & oxygen
- Neutral position
- Check for secretions, suction if needed 
- Put on oxygen
diagnoses.text2:
2. Check blood glucose
- If < 47 mg/dl or < 2.6 mmol/L give IV 10% glucose at 2ml/kg
- If blood glucose monitoring not available give IV 10% glucose at 2ml/kg
- Do full infection screen (blood culture, lumbar puncture, CRP if age is more than 36 hours)
- Take blood for Ca, Mg, U and E’s, FBC
diagnoses.text3:
3. Give anticonvulsants
- Give phenobarbitone 20mg/kg IM 
- Repeat loading dose ONCE if necessary
- If seizures ongoing give Phenytoin with a loading dose 20mg/kg  IV 
- If seizures still ongoing - give maintenance phenobarbitone 5mg/kg PO/IM

When seizures have stopped and baby stable click the blue arrow to continue

diagnoses.name: Dehydration
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby is >1 day old and showing signs of dehydration
diagnoses.text1:
Refer to WHO plan A, B or C as below:

Plan A

Give extra fluid orally:
Breastfeed frequently and for longer each feed
If infant vomits, wait 10 minutes then start again
If continues to vomit, will need clinic review
diagnoses.text2:
Plan B

Give 75ml/kg over 4 hours orally
Either by frequent breast feeds or cup feeds with EBM/formula
Reassess dehydration after 4 hours and select appropriate plan (A, B, C) to continue. 
If vomits, wait for 10 minutes then continue to offer feeds but more slowly
diagnoses.text3:
Plan C: Severe Dehydration


Give iv fluids10% dextrose or Ringers Lactate. 
Give first 30ml/kg in 1 hour, then 70ml/kg in 5 hours. 
Continue to offer breast/ cup feeds as tolerated

Reassess every 1-2 hours. If not improving, increase drip rate and check renal function
Monitor urine output
At 6 hours, reassess dehydration status and continue with plan A, B or C as appropriate

diagnoses.name: Difficulty Feeding
diagnoses.text1:
Below is a simple guide to feeding but please consult Iliff guidelines and wall charts for more detailed management 

1. Baby stable breathing <60bpm

If baby cannot feed adequately by breast or bottle but is stable, try using a cup or spoon 

Feed volumes day by day per kg are seen here.
diagnoses.text2:
2. Tachypnoea, breathing > 60bpm

If baby is breathing fast, tired or struggling to feed, insert a naso/orogastric tube and give feeds down the tube via syringe every 2 hours
diagnoses.text3:
3. Tachypnoea, breathing > 80bpm 

If baby is in significant distress, breathing over 80 times/minute or exhibiting other danger signs, stop feeds and begin IV fluids.

diagnoses.name: HIV Exposed
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: All HIV exposed infants should receive prophylaxis with triple therapy.
diagnoses.text1: MANAGEMENT
diagnoses.text2: FOR INFANTS UNDER 12 WEEKS OF AGE AND UNDER 2000G
diagnoses.text3:
TESTING AND OTHER

Infants should have a DNA PCR/NAT as soon as possible after delivery 
Results need to be chased as treatment needs to change if the baby tests positive

Prescribe Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis from 6 weeks of age until final confirmation of a negative HIV status (defined as a negative 18-month test or testing after breastfeeding ends if breastfed longer than 18 months)

diagnoses.name: Hypoglycaemia (symptomatic)
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Blood sugar below 47mgdL and showing symptoms
diagnoses.text1:
1. Give dextrose bolus 
- 2ml/kg of 10% dextrose IV over 5 minutes
- If no IV line feed baby via OGT/NGT as per feed chart
diagnoses.text2:
2. Give Maintenance fluids 

For fluid and rate see Wall Chart
diagnoses.text3: 3. Monitor Blood Glucose after 30 minutes

diagnoses.name: Hypoglycaemia (NOT symptomatic)
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Blood sugar below 47mgdL and NOT showing symptoms
diagnoses.text1:
1. Continue Breast Feeding or giving EBM by cup

- Monitor blood glucose 30 mins after feed
diagnoses.text2: 2. Increase frequency of feeds e.g. from 3 to 2 hourly or from 2 to 1 hourly
diagnoses.text3:
3. Monitor blood glucose before next feed or immediately if any symptoms!

- If 3 normal blood sugars (2.6 - 8.3mmol), monitoring can be stopped

diagnoses.name: Risk of hypoglycaemia
diagnoses.expressionMeaning:
Birth weight less than 2500g or greater than 4000g
Gestation less than 37wks
Mother has diabetes or received steroids
Baby admitted for Neonatal Encephalopathy
diagnoses.text1:
A baby presenting with any of the following conditions listed below is at risk of hypoglycaemia:
-	Birth weight <2500g
-	Birth weight >4000g
-	Infants of diabetic mothers
-	Preterm <37 weeks 
-	Maternal beta blocker use
-	Perinatal asphyxia, HIE, Neonatal encephalopathy
-	Late preterm exposure to antenatal steroids
diagnoses.text2:
Monitor blood sugars:
-	Ensure that baby is offered the breast within the first 60 minutes
-	Check blood glucose before the second feed (2-4 hours after birth)
-	If 3 normal blood sugars (>2.6 – 8.3mmol) on postnatal ward or NNU monitoring can be stopped
-	If blood sugar <2.6mmol (or < 47mgdL) follow the hypoglycaemia management pathway

diagnoses.name: Low Birth Weight (1500-2499g)
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby has weight of 1500g to 2499g
diagnoses.text1:
Manage this baby according to the weight as below:

Above 1800g:
- May require cup feeds
- Skin-skin & kangaroo care for thermoregulation
- If the baby is feeding well with assistance, warm and not exhibiting any danger signs, the baby can stay with their mother
- If the baby is not feeding well by breast, bottle, or cup or exhibiting any danger signs the baby should stay in neonatal unit
diagnoses.text2:
Less than 1799g:
- Needs admission to neonatal unit for close observation 
- 1500-1799g if not feeding well by breast start cup feeds
- Those <1500g should be fed by NGT and feeds advanced slowly as per the table

diagnoses.name: Possible Meconium Aspiration
diagnoses.text1:
Think - is this really Meconium aspiration?
Just because there was meconium at delivery doesn't mean it was aspirated! 
Most aspiration occurs in utero before the baby is born, so more likely if there was foetal distress
diagnoses.text2:
1. Airway and respiratory support

If baby FLOPPY with no respiratory effort:
- Intubate using direct laryngoscopy
- suction trachea applying suction to ET tube for 5 seconds maximum
- don''t repeat if no meconium retrieved.
- if heart rate <90 give gentle positive pressure ventilation and suction again later.

If baby VIGOROUS and breathing well:
Clear meconium from mouth and nose using large-bore suction catheter. Don't intubate

Continue normal resuscitation steps: drying, stimulating, repositioning and administering oxygen as necessary.
- If sats < 90% in air put on oxygen
diagnoses.text3:
2. Feeding support

- If breathing 60-80 bpm use cup/NGT
- If breathing > 80 bpm consider IV fluids 

3. IV Access for antibiotics 

Give X-penicillin and Gentamicin as per neonatal sepsis protocol

Minimal handling
Optimise temperature control

diagnoses.text2:

diagnoses.name: Normal Baby
diagnoses.text1:
Routine Care

1. Check if breast feeding well
2. Check if mother has been tested for HIV and refer for testing if HIV status unknown
3. Remind mothers to take infants to the local clinic for review at 3 days
4. Ensure baby has passed urine and stool in first 24 hours. 

If baby less than 24 hours old and has not passed urine or stool, ensure mother knows to seek a review locally or at HCH if stool/urine passage delayed beyond 24 hours.
diagnoses.text2:
Remember to check clinically for:

JAUNDICE 
Cataracts (red reflex)
Talipes: refer to orthopods/physio
Hip dysplasia
Extra digits
Heart murmurs
Anal atresia
diagnoses.text3:
Avoid unnecessary admission

Do not separate the mother from the infant if not absolutely necessary. Consider if observation may be sufficient without admission.

diagnoses.name: Pneumonia / Bronchiolitis
diagnoses.text1:
Consider risk factors (Same as for neonatal sepsis). 

Remember infections are often not localised and may spread rapidly

1. Airway and respiratory support

Position airway & suction
If sats < 90% in air put on oxygen
If > 1 kg consider CPAP according to TRY algorithm
diagnoses.text2:
2. Feeding support

If breathing 60-80 bpm use cup/NGT
If needing CPAP use OGT
If breathing > 80bpm consider IV fluids
diagnoses.text3:
3. Blood tests and antibiotics

Investigations: FBC including differential

Blood cultures- take BEFORE commencing antibiotics if possible
Remember to write the Neotree number on the bottle and form (first 3 and last 3 digits of full number)

Lumbar puncture if signs of meningism
CRP if available. 

Commence: X pen 50000 iu/kg/dose 12 hourly
gentamicin 5 mg/kg/dose 24 hourly 

Reduce gentamicin to 4 mg/kg/dose if <2000g

Stop at 48 hours if Cultures/investigations negative AND symptoms resolved.

diagnoses.name: Premature (32 to 37 weeks)
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby's gestation is 32 weeks to 36 weeks
diagnoses.text1:
Most stable larger preterm babies (>1500g) not needing oxygen may safely be nursed with their mother in Kangaroo Care. 
Remember to perform Ballard Score- images are for neuromuscular followed by physical maturity assessment  - (Ballad score images in script)
diagnoses.text2:
WARM CHAIN is maintained: 
•	Keep the radiant warmer or resucitaire on
•	For babies < 32 weeks deliver into plastic bag before drying if available. If not, dry infant in warm 
towel and wrap in another dry warm towel.
•	Put skin to skin with mother and cover both with blanket
•	Keep room/transport incubator/ambulance (if transporting) as warm as possible.
•	Ensure baby has a hat & socks, and perform procedures in the incubator.

1. Thermoregulation
Keep the baby warm aiming between 36.5-37.5’C by Skin to skin (KMC position) or place on radiant warmer or incubator if available

Mild hypothermia: 36-36.4 --> cause for concern,  warm the baby

Moderate hypothermia: 32-35.9--> DANGER
•	rewarm baby,  
•	check blood glucose

Severe hypothermia <32, outcome likely to be poor, 
•	rewarm baby, 
•	check blood glucose

2. Respiratory support
•	Oxygen / CPAP
•	CPAP >28 weeks or > 1000g and passes the TRY CPAP algorithm (image in script)
•	Remember preterms may have slightly reduced tone due to their prematurity
•	Early CPAP for babies between 28 - 32 weeks
•	Prevention of apnoea Give Caffeine Citrate 20mg/kg orally or slowly by intravenous route over 30 minutes and a maintenance dose of 5mg/kg/day to all preterm babies<32 weeks. Give until 34 weeks postnestrual age.
•	If Caffeine citrate is not available give a loading dose of aminophylline at 6mg/kg over 20 minutes followed by a maintenance dose of 2.5mg/kg every 12 hours
diagnoses.text3:
3. Feeding support 
•	If able to suck GIVE breast feed
•	If not able to suck give cup feeds or consider OGT 
•	OGT for all babies < 1500g, RR > 60 and needing respiratory support
•	OGT if on CPAP
•	Consider IV fluids in smaller babies breathing > 80 bpm

diagnoses.name: Transient Tachypnoea of Newborn (TTN)
diagnoses.text1:
These babies are not unwell 
RR is usually between 60-80 breaths per minute & don''t need oxygen
This should resolve in 6 hours.
TTN is more likely following elective C-section due to wet lungs

1. Airway and respiratory support

- If sats < 90% in air put on oxygen. Diagnosis is unlikely TTN! 
- Position airway in neutral and suction if necessary
diagnoses.text2:
2. Feeding support

Babies with TTN are likely to need cup/NGT until RR < 60
diagnoses.text3:
3. Antibiotics are not needed!

If the Tachypnoea continues longer than 6 hours or any other signs/symptoms develop e.g. fever then it is unlikely TTN and might be sepsis so start antibiotics.

diagnoses.name: Premature baby with Respiratory Distress
diagnoses.expression: $Gestation < 37 and ($RR > 60 or $DangerSigns = 'Grun' or $DangerSigns = 'Cyan' or $SatsAIr < 90 or $SatsO2 < 90 or $RespSR = 'DIB' or $RespSR = 'BE' or $RespSR = 'Apn' or $RespSR = 'Cough' or $RespSR = 'NBr' or $SignsRD = 'TT' or $SignsRD = 'NFL' or $SignsRD = 'CHI' or $SignsRD = 'HN' or $SignsRD = 'ST' or $SignsRD = 'GR' or $SignsRD = 'Gasp' or $SignsRD = 'GR')
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Gestation is less than 37 weeks and baby showed one of the signs/risks of respiratory distress.
diagnoses.text1:
Care must be given to thermoregulation as per preterm guidelines
Remember to perform Ballard Score

1. Airway and Respiratory support 
Position the airway in neutral
If saturations < 90% put on oxygen
If distress is significant and > 1kg consider CPAP according to the TRY CPAP algorithm.
Start on Caffeine if baby is less than 34 weeks old or less than 1500g 
Consider surfactant if >1000g with severe respiratory distress requiring CPAP and an oxygen requirement FiO2>35%
diagnoses.text2:
2. Feeding support 

If breathing 60-80 bpm use cup/OGT
If needing CPAP use OGT
If breathing > 80 bpm consider IV fluids
diagnoses.text3:
3. Get IV access, take blood culture and start antibiotics 

Antibiotics are recommended in preterm babies with RDS if they have signs of sepsis or risk factors for sepsis as listed in the EDLIZ sepsis table.

Commence:
Benzylpenicillin 
50,000-100 000 IU/kg 12 hourly IV/IM (use higher dose if seriously unwell or concerns about CNS infection/meningitis)
Increase frequency to 8 hourly in second week of life and then to 6 hourly at 14 days (term) or 28 days (preterm) 

AND 

Gentamicin
Birth weight less than 2kg: 5 mg/kg
      • Less than 1 kg: 48 hourly dosing for first two weeks, then 36 hr dosing
      • Birth weight1-2 kg: less than 1 week old 48 hourly dosing, greater than 1 week 36 hr
Birth weight greater than 2kg: 4mg/kg 
       • Less than 1 week old: 24hr dosing,
       • More than 1 week old: 24 – 48 hr dosing

diagnoses.name: Term with Respiratory Distress
diagnoses.expression: $Gestation >= 37 and ($RR > 60 or $DangerSigns = 'Grun' or $DangerSigns = 'Cyan' or $SatsAIr < 90 or $SatsO2 < 90 or $RespSR = 'DIB' or $RespSR = 'BE' or $RespSR = 'Apn' or $RespSR = 'Cough' or $RespSR = 'NBr' or $SignsRD = 'TT' or $SignsRD = 'HN' or $SignsRD = 'ST' or $SignsRD = 'NFL' or $SignsRD = 'CHI' or $SignsRD = 'GR' or $SignsRD = 'Gasp' or $SignsRD = 'GR')

diagnoses.text1:
Position airway in neutral 
Apply nasal prong oxygen to maintain saturations 90-95%
Consider CPAP as per TRY CPAP algorithm  if > 1kg and good tone and if the RR>60, Room oxygen saturations are < 90% or if there are retractions and grunting per flowchart below.
diagnoses.text2:

If NOT on CPAP use cup/OGT feeding until RR<60 bpm
OGT for all babies < 1500g, RR > 60 and needing respiratory support
OGT if on CPAP
Consider IV fluids if respiratory rate > 80 bpm
diagnoses.text3:
3. Antibiotics:  - If respiratory distress started greater than 4 hours old (if there are no other conditions requiring antibiotics earlier than 4 hours old) and ongoing respiratory distress:
Take blood culture before starting antibiotics

Maintain normothermia
Encourage and support breast feeding

Start antibiotics -covering for meningitis

diagnoses.name: Suspected neonatal sepsis
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: EDLIZ table; 1 Major OR 2 Minor Criteria
diagnoses.text1:
Summary
1. Perform blood cultures PRIOR to giving antibiotics if possible
REMEMBER TO WRITE NEOTREE NUMBER ON BLOOD CULTURE BOTTLE

2. Antibiotics
All babies with suspected sepsis should receive intravenous antibiotics.

If antibiotics are started in the first 48 hours of life use:
X-pen/Benzylpenicillin and Gentamicin.
See full guideline below for dosing and duration.

If the baby becomes unwell at over 48 hours of age: 
Use Ampicillin and Amikacin if available. If Ampicillin and Amikacin are not available, use cloxacillin and gentamicin.
See full guideline below for dosing.

Even if there are no risk factors for sepsis on admission, babies should be reassessed for signs of sepsis daily during admission.

3. Supportive care
Check blood sugar and provide feeding support if needed
 
Give 2-3 ml/kg 10% dextrose bolus if blood glucose <2.6mmol/dl and baby symptomatic
 
Give 10ml/kg fluid bolus if shocked (0.9% Sodium Chloride or Ringers Lactate)
 
Thermoregulation: aim for body temperature between 36.5 - 37.5
 
If baby has fever (T = 38.5) remove from warmer and unwrap 
 
Provide respiratory support as needed
diagnoses.text2:
Full guideline for reference:
1. Perform cultures PRIOR to giving antibiotics if possible
REMEMBER TO WRITE NEOTREE NUMBER ON BLOOD CULTURE BOTTLE

Follow the unit blood culture taking guidelines, with special care to minimise contamination and ensure an adequate blood volume in the bottle (1-2ml).

If it is impossible to perform the culture, antibiotics should not be delayed, but this is sub-optimal medicine.
If the suspicion of meningitis is strong, one should perform lumbar puncture before starting antibioticsif possible.

2. Antibiotics
If antibiotics are started in the first 48 hours use:

Benzylpenicillin
100,000IU/kg 12 hourly IV/IM
Increase frequency to 8 hourly in second week of life and then 6 hourly at 14 days (term) or 28 days (preterm)

AND

Gentamicin
Birth weight less than 2kg: 5mg/kg
•	Less than 1kg: 48 hourly dosing for first two weeks, then 36 hourly dosing
•	1-2kg less than 1 week old 48 hourly dosing, greater than 1 week 36 hr

Birth weight greater than 2kg: 4mg/kg
•	Less than 1 week: 24hr dosing
•	More than 1 week: 24 – 48 hr dosing

NB: Increase dose interval by 12 hr if at risk of Acute Kidney Injury (e.g HIE or patient on other nephrotoxic drugs). Perform a gentamicin trough level before every third dose. Monitor urine output and renal function in babies who remain on aminoglycosides.

(NB Ampicillin is an alternative to Benzylpenicillin - see dosing below)

If there are concerns of cellulitis/arthritis or osteomyelitis then use Cloxacillin and Gentamicin.
Stop Gentamicin if blood culture excludes Gram negative organism.

Cloxacillin dose 30-50mg/kg (use 100mg/kg if osteitis or intracranial infection)
1st week of life: 12h
2nd to 4th week of life: 8h

If baby becomes unwell AFTER 48 hours of age use:

Ampicillin 50-100mg/kg twice daily IV for first week of life, increase to 8 hourly from 7-20 days, increase to 6 hourly from 21-28 days. Use higher dose in vey severe infections or suspected meningitis.

AND Amikacin 15mg/kg once daily IV

If Ampicillin and Amikacin are not available use:

Cloxacillin 30-50mg/kg. 1st week of life 12 hourly. 2nd to 4th week of life 8 hourly.

AND Gentamicin 
Less than 2kg Birth weight: 5mg/kg
 •        Less than 1kg: 48 hourly dosing for first two weeks, then 36 hourly dosing
•        1-2kg less than 1 week old 48 hourly dosing, greater than 1 week 36 hr
Greater than 2kg birth weight: 4mg/kg
•        Less than 1 week: 24hr dosing
•        More than 1 week: 24 – 48 hr dosing
diagnoses.text3:
Duration of antibiotics
Most babies who have empirical antibiotics started for suspected sepsis do not in fact have an infection and should have their antibiotics stopped at 36-48h if they fulfil all these criteria:

1. No growth has been obtained on the blood culture so far
2. The CRP level done at 36-48h is normal (if available)
3. The baby does not have clinical signs of sepsis

Babies with a positive blood culture should have an LP done. If there is no meningitis antibiotics should be continued for at least 7-10 days, and only terminated when the child is well. If CRP is being monitored ensure it has normalised before stopping antibiotics.

If the child has Gram-positive meningitis (including GBS or Staphylococcus aureus) or Staphylococcus aureus septicaemia continue antibiotics for at least 14 days.

If Gram negative meningitis ( E.coli or Klebsiella) continue antibiotics for at least 21 days

3. Antibiotics

Start triple antibiotics
1. Ampicillin (25-50mg/kg IV BD, consult unit guidelines) and
2. Amikacin (15mg/kg IV once a day if < 4 weeks old);

diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby has a small sac protruding from the back or the head
diagnoses.text1:
1. Handle with sterile, latex-free gloves (if possible) and sterile towels at delivery

Nurse side-lying or prone to ensure no pressure is placed on the lesion
Wrap lesion with sterile gauze soaked in warm saline
diagnoses.text2:
2. Antibiotics

Apply topical tetracycline and give IV Benzylpenicillin (100-150 mg/kg daily in two divided doses) or Ampicillin (25-50 mg/kg IM or IV four times a day) PLUS Amikacin for 5 days

Refer to Paediatric Neurosurgeon for closure.
diagnoses.text3:
3. Monitoring

Monitor daily head circumference  and obtain Cranial USS and CT (if CrUSS is of concern and possible) 
Monitor for symptoms of bowel, bladder and motor deficit and hydrocephalus (apnoea, bradycardia, hypoventilation, stridor, swallow dysfunction) 

Monitor urine output and obtain renal ultrasound (if possible). Check Creatine Day 5 to 7

Results need to be chased as treatment needs to change if the baby tests positive

Prescribe Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis from 6 weeks of age until final confirmation of a negative HIV status (defined as a negative 18-month test or testing after breastfeeding ends if breastfed longer than 18 months)

managementMetadata.contentText:
Prepare this baby for referral according to instructions below.

Keep the baby on oxygen if available
If oxygen is NOT available CALL referral hospital immediately for guidance and if Possible send the baby with accompanying health worker with Bag and Mask Ventilation (BMV) equipment.

Continue with the Neotree examination.
managementMetadata.title: Referral Instructions (O2)
managementMetadata.text1:
1. Assess Airway, breathing and circulation
2. Ensure baby is on Oxygen IF AVAILABLE 
3. Keep Warm - place hat and wrap baby
4. Manage any other emergency signs - including convulsions
5. Review by senior clinician or nurse - if available
6. Give stat doses of antibiotics - Xpen and Gentamicin
7. Consider need for 2ml/kg 10% dextrose bolus and need for IV fluids for transfer if appropriate and safe.
managementMetadata.text2:
1. Inform receiving facility (SMCH) of case summary by phone call - discuss availability of portable Oxygen & medical escort
2. Communicate to guardian intention to refer and reasons
3. Attach Neotree print out ready for transit
4. Attach all relevant documents/ notes/ checks (glucose, HIV, VDRL, X-rays, lab results etc.)
managementMetadata.text3:
1. Put baby on portable Oxygen IF AVAILABLE
2. Refer in KMC unless clinical conditions require observation & care in transit
3. Refer with escort (Nurse or clinician) with BMV  equipment - IF AVAILABLE
4. Nurse or clinician to bring emergency supplies in ambulance (bag & mask, penguin sucker, dextrose etc.)
5. IN PERSON handover by nurse or clinician at receiving facility

managementMetadata.contentText: Sterility is key in the management of these babies and preventing meningitis and severe sepsis  - this significantly improves their outcome
managementMetadata.title: Referral Instructions - Diagnoses requiring Neurological surgical management
managementMetadata.text1:
1. Assess ABC
2. Keep baby warm
3. Maintain a sterile, latex-free environment
4. Place the baby in a side-lying position to avoid pressure on the back lesion.
5. Wrap the lesion in a sterile, saline-soaked gauze with an occlusive plastic wrap
managementMetadata.text2:
1. If large defect: Broad spectrum antibiotics : Benzylpenicillin, Metronidazole and Gentamicin
2. This baby needs URGENT neurosurgical review - These babies can be born with significant hydrocephalus depending on severity of the defect
3. Transfer in KMC unless clinical conditions require observation & care in transit
4. Refer with escort (Nurse or clinician) - IF AVAILABLE
5. Nurse or clinician to bring emergency supplies in ambulance (bag & mask, penguin sucker, dextrose etc.)
6. IN PERSON handover at receiving facility

screens.title: Referral Instructions - Diagnoses requiring Abdominal surgical management

managementMetadata.contentText:
These babies need stabilisation PRIOR to transfer  - this significantly improves their outcome

Aim to leave and transfer this baby within an hour!
managementMetadata.title: Referral Instructions - Diagnoses requiring Abdominal surgical management
managementMetadata.text1:
1. Assess ABC
2. Keep baby warm
3. Wrap bowel in clingfilm or sterile bag up to armpit - to minimise fluid loss
4. Nil By Mouth and insert NGT for aspiration on free drainage
5. Insert cannula and give 20 mL/kg of normal saline or Hartmann’s solution as a bolus
6. Start IV Fluids at 60mls/kg/day  - 10% Dextrose
7. Monitor blood sugar
managementMetadata.text2:
1. Start triple antibiotics
          a. Ampicillin (25-50mg/kg IV four times a day) and
          b. Amikacin (15mg/kg IV once a day if < 4 weeks old); 
              - if unavailable: Gentamicin: <2kg Birth weight : use 5 mg kg/dose or >2kg birth weight : use 4mg/kg dose
          c. Metronidazole (15mg/kg as a single loading dose, followed by 7.5mg/kg every 12hr starting 24 hr after the loading dose)
2. Transfer in KMC unless clinical conditions require observation & care in transit
3. Refer with escort (Nurse or clinician) - IF AVAILABLE
4. Nurse or clinician to bring emergency supplies in ambulance (bag & mask, penguin sucker, dextrose etc.)
5. IN PERSON handover at receiving facility
managementMetadata.text3:
1. Inform receiving facility (SMCH) of case summary by Phone - discuss availability of medical escort
2. Communicate to guardian intention to refer and reasons - Counsel and educate parents - encourage parental bonding
3. Attach Neotree print out ready for transfer
4. Attach all relevant documents/ notes/ checks (glucose, HIV, VDRL, X-rays, lab results etc.)
